question: A wheel makes 500 revolutions in covering a distance of 44 km. Find the radius of the wheel.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Radius (r)** = [**Total Distance**] ÷ [2 × π × **Revolutions**]

Distance = 44 km = 44,000 m.

r = 44,000 ÷ (2 × 22/7 × 500)

r = (44,000 × 7) ÷ (44 × 500)

r = 1,000 × 7 ÷ 500 = 14 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Total Distance** = 44 km, **Number of Revolutions** = 500.

**Formula:** **Distance** = **Number of Revolutions** × **Circumference** (2πr)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/56d60db1b5b5f41ef822de81ff031ac9fea337472ecae080bd880fbfc156b6ca.png] 

⇒ **Total Distance** = 44 × 1000 = 44,000 m

⇒ **Distance covered in 1 revolution** = 44,000 ÷ 500

⇒ **Circumference (2πr)** = 88 m

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 88

⇒ (44/7) × r = 88

⇒ r = (88 × 7) ÷ 44

⇒ r = 2 × 7 = 14 m

**∴ The correct answer is 14 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circumference of a Circle

The distance around the edge of a circle is calculated as C = 2πr or C = πd, where r is the **radius** and d is the **diameter**.

Distance and Revolutions

For any rolling wheel, the **Total Distance** covered is always equal to the **Number of Revolutions** × **Circumference**.

Unit Conversion

Always ensure units are consistent; 1 kilometer (km) = 1000 meters (m) and 1 meter (m) = 100 centimeters (cm).</p
